reason: Every observation reproduces and the conclusion drawn from them is still wrong, so the fix is wrong too. Reproduced first: driven in chromium at 1440 at ?state=first-run with an addInitScript setter rewriting the fixture's live week from 12 to 3 before render, the hero printed 3, the mark printed '3 so far', the spoken line said 3, --h was still 100, the bar still painted 168px in a 168px plot, and all three assertions at interaction-check.mjs:941-943 returned PASS. lately.html:1002 does write the literal --h:100, and the `value: f.weeks.at(-1).v` read at :936 is dead — nothing compares it. So the assertion is misnamed. It is not vacuous. WHY THE CONSEQUENCE COLLAPSES. The finding says 'if the first-run mark's height ever decouples from its value, 461 assertions pass and nobody is told.' The height is decoupled from its value BY DESIGN and must be. lately.html:281-285 says so in the source: 'a gridline derived from a single datum labels the datum with itself. So there is no scale here, because there is not one.' A solo week is its own maximum, so the derived height pct(v, max) is exactly 100 for EVERY possible fixture value. There is no relation to hold down, and no failure mode going unreported. The assertion's real subject is 'the solo mark fills its plot', and it does fail on the only thing that can break that — edit the 100 to a 50 and it goes red. That is source-sensitive, unlike the genuinely vacuous class this round has been finding (a predicate true regardless of the source). Misnamed guard, not an unfailable one. WHY THE FIX IS WRONG, part by part. (c) 'painted mark height equals painted plot height within 1px' is condemned by the finding's own standard: it also cannot fail for any fixture value and fails only when the literal is edited — identical failure power to `plot.h === 100`. It renames the flaw, it does not remove it. (d) 'assert lately.html writes --h as an interpolation of D, not a bare digit' mandates an interpolation that is provably the constant 100 for every input — pure ceremony — and it asks the source to pretend to a scale the CSS comment deliberately refuses; it also drops an HTML-source regex into a runtime browser gate, the exact brittleness two other briefs this round are already about. (e) is factually wrong about the source: `.colw` has NO max-width — computed `none` — the 22px cap lives on `.bar`. Measured at 1440, the full state's .colw is 50.66px and moves with the viewport while the solo bar is 22px, so binding the solo mark's width to a .colw max-width binds it to a property that does not exist and to a number it would never equal. SEVERITY IS OVERSTATED. Nothing on the surface is wrong in any state or under a mutated fixture; the class is refinement, not defect. What survives is small and real: nothing in the gate binds the first-run printed numerals to the fixture — kept in sharpenedFix.
sharpenedFix: Do not derive the height and do not regex the HTML. Rename the assertion to what it actually guards and add the one binding that is genuinely missing. (1) Rename `the first-run mark's height comes from its value, not a literal` to `the solo mark fills its plot, because one week is its own maximum` and keep `plot.h === 100` — that is the invariant, and it is the correct one. Rewrite the block comment to match: the r1 fix was the pitch and the spoken value, not a derived height. (2) Spend the dead `value` read: assert the printed mark and the hero numeral both read the fixture's live week — `document.querySelector('.bar-val').textContent.trim() === `${plot.value} so far`` and `document.querySelector('.t-hero').textContent.trim() === String(plot.value)`. Nothing in the gate does this today; the single-accessor design (both interpolate D.thisWeek) makes disagreement unlikely, so this is a cheap regression pin, not a defect being caught. (3) Tighten the loose width ceiling to the real cap rather than to a .colw: read the full state's `.plot .bar` width in the same run and assert the solo bar equals it — both measure 22px at 1440, set by `.bar { max-width: 22px }`, and `<= 60` can only fail if that rule is deleted AND the container widens. Verify each new line against the current source (must pass) and against a source with the numeral edited (must fail) before it lands.
breaks: Nothing on the surface — this is gate-side only. After it lands, re-run interaction-check.mjs across all seven states and confirm the count moves from 461 to 463 with no reds; confirm the renamed assertion still trips when lately.html:1002 is edited from --h:100 to --h:50, and that the two new value assertions trip when the hero interpolation is changed to a literal. Do NOT adopt (d): a source-text regex over lately.html would go stale the moment the template is reformatted, and it would force a derived height that is constant by construction. Re-measure the .bar width assertion at 390/768/1280/1440 before trusting the equality — .bar is capped at 22px so it should hold, but the full state's .colw is viewport-dependent and must not be the anchor.
